sections.title: OpenRouter provider class
sections.what: Implements the common provider contract for OpenRouter. It checks for a key, builds and sends a chat request over the web, and turns the reply into the standard shape.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives access to many models through one adapter without new code for each model.
sections.watch_out: Failures are thrown with only the first 300 characters of the response, so some error detail is lost.

summary: Adapter that calls the OpenRouter web API directly to send chat requests to models from many providers.
purpose: Gives the router a second provider, used through the same contract as OpenAI.
why: Likely reason: one key can reach many models. Not otherwise stated.
how: 1. Checks that the OPENROUTER_API_KEY setting exists. 2. Removes an openrouter/ prefix from the model name. 3. Builds the request body, adding temperature, length limit and JSON format when set. 4. Sends it to OpenRouter with the app's referrer and title. 5. Throws an error containing the first 300 characters of the response if the call fails. 6. Returns the text, model name and token counts.
inputs: A model name, the chat messages and optional settings, plus the API key from the environment.
outputs: A standard model reply, or an error.
risks: No time limit is set on the web request, so a stalled call can hang. The referrer and title identify the app to OpenRouter. The key is read from the environment on every call.
debug: Look in the logs for OpenRouter API error followed by a status code. A 401 usually means a bad key and a 429 usually means rate limiting. Confirm OPENROUTER_API_KEY is set and check the model name spelling.
